notes:
Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-7b31c4, issue #1327, 23 September 2026, completing the checkpoint merged earlier the same day. Source read: the author's version on V. Pilloni's homepage (17 June 2019, 113 pp.), whose recorded sha256 4c05724efeab1dbbb108f980ec9a722127d2a8cd2abf6e8c2a6a2251cf0f9f58 reproduces byte for byte. The published Duke text is paywalled and was not compared, as the extraction states; every locator is a page and statement number of the author version, and that boundary is right and should stay.

Findings. All 175 sourceIssues now carry verdicts and all 175 are confirmed: 11 errors, 21 gaps, 143 misprints. Nothing was rejected, nothing was deleted, and I added no finding of my own. For each I located the quoted text on the page its locator gives and checked the correction against the paper's own conventions; where the correction is a computation I redid it, and several are decided by internal evidence the extraction did not cite. The three sharpest: the BGG equivariance exponent of Proposition 13.3.3.1 (E119) is settled by Corollary 13.3.3.1's own bounds, since -3 + (k+1) = k-2 and 0 + (k+1) = k+1 are exactly the slopes it asserts, whereas the printed p^{-k-1} would give -k-4 and -k-1; the Serre-Tate exponents on p. 60 (E77) are settled by running the same commutativity computation on the paper's own analogue on p. 39, which reproduces the relations printed there; and the Dieudonne Frobenius matrix on p. 35 (E49) is incompatible with the symplectic form J of section 5.1, since the pair e_2, e_3 gives <Fe_2,Fe_3> = -p against the required +p.

Six findings were recorded in my checkpoint as image-only. Improving the local text extractor to decode the TeX OML, OMS, OT1 and MSBM font encodings made Greek letters, arrows and relation symbols legible in the text layer, and all six then checked directly: E56 (the Ha labels on the vertical arrows), E62 (the upright 00 for oo), E92 (the index placement), E95 (kappa for k), E121 (the weight in the spectral-variety display) and E133 (the a-exponents in the first diagram of Corollary 14.6.1). Three items still rest on the extraction's renders rather than on my own reading, and I say so in each verdict: the K_p versus K^p subscripts of E34, the citation string "chap. 23, thm. 2.3.1" of E76, and the Narasimhan spelling in E174. In each the surrounding argument is decisive independently of the glyph.

Overlaps, all consistent, none contradictory. Several findings are recorded twice, once alone and once inside a bundle: E83 is the first item of E81; E137 is the misprint half of E134 and E138 the index half of E135; E93 and E95 are items of E89; E172 and E175 are items of E168; E166 shares its entry with E170 and E171 with E169; E54 and E55 share the p. 43 slip; E35 and E37 share the p. 28 base; E114 is noted in passing inside E116; E121 and E123 are the notational and mathematical halves of one display; E139 is the "positive valuation" half of E141. I confirmed each on its own terms and cross-referenced them in the verdicts rather than deleting any, since each is correct and the bundles carry context the singletons do not.

Two small slips are printed and no finding records them: "Morover" for "Moreover" on p. 92, and "pi_infinity in an irreducible" for "is an irreducible" in Theorem 15.2.2.1(2) on p. 108. Both are typographical and I leave them for a later pass rather than manufacture findings.

Structure, re-verified in full and unchanged. 550 items (485 missing, 59 planned, 6 library) and 25 routes: 19 source, 5 Part II, 1 new. Every missing item is routed exactly once. All 19 source stage ids resolve in data/atlas.json. Of the 133 planned references, the 123 of Stage:Layer form all resolve there; the other 10 use the corpus-wide tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/...#layer-... form, whose targets live in the Tau Ceti repository and cannot be resolved from this one. All five Part II titles reproduce their parents' atlas titles exactly, all six route areas are galaxy ids (padic, automorphic, langlands, arithmeticgeometry, langlands, arithmeticgeometry), and the one new roadmap id GSp4NonregularModularityLifting is free. Each claimed join checks out against the corpus: SiegelModularFormsModPn and GSp4NonregularModularityLifting against PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20, IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes against PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18, ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII against PAPER-KISIN-MADAPUSIPERA-SHIN-22 and eight others, ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary against PAPER-FARB-KISIN-WOLFSON-24; and route 1's claim to be this paper's own proposal rather than a join is right, since PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-21, -25 and PAPER-BOXER-PILLONI-26 all carry the identical id, parent, title and area and each names PAPER-PILLONI-20 as the proposal it joins.

One correction made in place. The extraction recorded no libraryPins, although all 43 declarations behind its six library items resolve at the standing pins. I added libraryPins with mathlib 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174 and tauceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369 and re-checked all 43 against the declaration index at those commits. What this review did not do. I did not read all 113 pages line by line; I read the pages every finding names, the statements the routes cite, and the surrounding sections needed to judge them. I did not compare the published Duke text. scripts/check_paper.py and research/blueprint/intake.py check-files both pass on the result file.
